analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (new head lines 516-533, a 'Nemotron Super component qualification' section) and docs/provider/direct-mode.md (new lines ~179-214, an 'Experimental Nemotron Super owner fixtures' section). No source, config or workflow change is visible, and no controls were altered.

The docs describe an optional NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP owner hook in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Server/NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift. Claimed properties: default absent, no production callsite installs it, no new model advertised, and it reuses existing local auth, body limits and cancellation scope. When installed it accepts inline PNG/JPEG data URIs, with the format chosen by content rather than the label, and it returns 400/422/429 for the listed bad inputs. Concurrency defaults to one request. Image input is refused when MTP is installed.

This is relevant to A-001, TB-003, TB-007 and T-050. The related threat T-050 covers plaintext media exposure. The docs say 'Cancellation must retain media/KV and response ownership until native terminal retirement', which is a stated requirement, not a verifiable property.

Unverified, because the implementation was not supplied: (1) local auth and body limits on the new hook; (2) image decode bounds, decompression-bomb limits, and whether the image path writes temp files (T-050); (3) cancellation and drain behavior; (4) the hook's data-handling behavior in the path from the local HTTP server (which TB-002 does not cover).

This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The threat model has no entry for the hook. If a production callsite is added, the threat model needs updating, for example for media parsing, local-HTTP access and concurrency DoS. The docs claim that the hook is not production-installed and that this is not production qualification, so the threat model needs no change now.
